title: LD-Scene: LLM-guided diffusion for controllable generation of adversarial safety-critical driving scenarios

control_signal.value: Natural-language user query naming the adversarial vehicle, collision type and adversarial collision severity (weak/medium/strong adversarial level).

control_mechanism.value: An LLM chain-of-thought code generator plus LLM debugger turn the query into a guidance loss function; the loss steers the latent denoising sampling at inference (inference-time guidance).

base_model.value: Latent diffusion model (U-Net denoiser) on a pretrained graph-based VAE from Strive with frozen encoders and autoregressive kinematic decoder; GPT-4o used for code generator and debugger.

datasets.value: nuScenes (train split for training, validation split for evaluation); 2 s past to predict 6 s future.

metrics.value: Adv-Ego collision rate, Adv acceleration, adversary/other off-road rates, Adv-Other/Other-Ego/Other-Other collision rates, closed-loop Sim Time; TTC and lateral/longitudinal acceleration for adversarial level.

controllability_evidence.value: Table 1: Adv-Ego Coll 40.75% vs 27.81% for Safe-Sim. Adversarial level weak/medium/strong gives TTC 2.06/1.98/1.91 s and Adv Acc_lon 1.02/1.09/1.20 m/s2. Three query case studies (normal, high-speed, sharp-turn collision).

notes: Strong level collision rate (39.33%) is not above medium (40.75%); authors attribute this to missed collision timing in low-speed interactions. Limitations section not in packet.
